newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico arrests traffickers of deaf workers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico arrests traffickers of deaf workers.

text.p: Mexican authorities arrested the suspected ringleader of the group that trafficked in deaf Mexicans and forced them to work in the United States for slave wages, the Federal Attorney General's Office (PGR) said late on Thursday.
Mexico-based international police arrested four people in Mexico City on Thursday afternoon, including suspected leader Reinaldo Paoletti and members of his family, the PGR said in a statement.

On July 18, about 60 deaf and mute Mexican immigrants were found in New York City held in servitude and forced to peddle trinkets on the street. Other disabled Mexicans were later uncovered under similar conditions in Sanford, North Carolina, Chicago and Detroit.
The four were arrested Thursday afternoon when two of them entered a bank to cash in 1.7 million pesos, the PGR said.
The police later found father and son, Jose Paoletti Moreda and Renato Paoletti Lemus, in a house in Mexico City, the PGR said. It said the two are deaf and mute.
"At this time the arrested people are making a declaration, the disabled ones through the help of a special translator," the PGR said.
At least eight people have already been arrested in connection with the exploitation, including other members of the Paoletti family in the United States.
Officials believe the ringleaders lured the deaf and mute Mexicans from their homes with the promise of a better life in the United States.
